Thanks for the 30-min call today — quick recap + asks so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private.

Summary of Atlas Retail needs:
- Primary workload: checkout assist + cart personalization chat invoked on high-traffic flows
- Traffic profile: baseline ~40 TPS; promotional peaks ~300 TPS sustained 5-15 mins; burst spikes to 600 TPS.
- Token mix (typical): avg prompt 90 tokens; avg completion 320 tokens; 95th pct completion ~900 tokens on long assists.
- SLO: p95 end-to-end latency target ~200ms for simple prompts; acceptable up to 400ms for long assists.
- Data residency: US-only; prefer VPC network for PCI-adjacent subsystems.

Immediate questions we discussed:
1) Hosted API: fastest to test but likely requires tiered fallback during peaks.
2) Dedicated: best for predictable throughput and isolation — need guidance on #GPUs (H100 vs A100), per-GPU concurrency, and batching.
3) Private (VPC/on‑prem): possible later for stricter compliance; upfront CAPEX concerns.

Attachments: atlas-sizing-workbook-v2.xlsx (workbook for you to fill traffic windows + sample payloads), redwood-dedicated-options.pdf (rough GPU configs).

Next asks:
- Jordan: can you drop a sample of 50 anonymized conversation payloads (varied lengths) into the workbook?
- Confirm whether 95th token lengths are representative or if 900 tokens is a rare outlier.
- Is there a preferred budget range for monthly committed capacity?

I'll loop in Ben to sketch sizing options based on the numbers above; aim to have a recommendation within 48 hours.

Jordan — thanks. See two pragmatic sizing options below based on the traffic and token mix you shared.

---Quoted text from Jordan Miller---
> Our peaks are typically sustained 10–12 minutes during promotions; 300 TPS conservative, up to 500 TPS for a few minutes.

Sizing options (estimates; final numbers require sample traces):
Option 1 — Performance-first (Recommended for strict p95 latency targets):
- Hardware: 4x H100 (NVLink-enabled cluster)
- Expected sustained TPS: ~350 TPS (prompt 90 / completion 320 avg)
- Peak handling with autoscale/burst: spikes to ~600 TPS with short warmup + pre-warming policies
- p95 token-generation latency: ~80–130ms depending on prompt; end-to-end p95 ~150–220ms
- Concurrency model: medium (16–32 concurrent streams per GPU) with batching window tuned to 8–12ms
- Notes: higher upfront commit cost; best headroom for spikes and KV-heavy sessions.

Option 2 — Cost-optimized (If budget constrained):
- Hardware: 8x A100 (more cards, lower per-card perf)
- Expected sustained TPS: ~220–300 TPS
- Peak handling: slower to ramp; p95 token-gen higher ~120–220ms; end-to-end ~220–350ms
- Concurrency: higher threads per GPU but larger batching to keep utilization
- Notes: lower monthly commit vs H100 option; may need fallback to Hosted for extreme short spikes.

KV cache and request coalescing impact:
- Effective TPS can improve ~15–35% for workloads with repeated prefixes (cart/session level caching).
- For chat sessions with long KV usage, H100 option retains larger KV-resident state enabling fewer KV-evictions and lower tail latency.

Next steps I suggest:
- Workshop (45 min) where Atlas provides a 1-hour sample trace (anonymized) — we will run a quick perf pass and return a refined workbook.
- If you approve, I'll schedule the workshop and provision a temporary dedicated test cluster (ephemeral) to validate.
